A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlowSearch. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including the substantially replaced report-generation example.

before.justification: v1 reports original FlowSearch benchmark results, component and planner ablations, and execution case studies in Section 3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and ablations in Section 4, revises several results, and presents case-study outputs in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The DAG representation, incremental planner, knowledge collector, six refinement operations, and dual-mode conclusion generation are retained. Expanded explanations of parallel execution and local graph revision do not establish a changed procedure; Appendix C's planner training description is identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GAIA, GPQA-diamond, HLE, and TRQA-lit and retain the same question-answering and report-generation case-study queries. Different subjects discussed inside the replacement generated report do not constitute additional evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds WebDancer, WebShaper, MiroThinker, Tongyi DR, JoyAgent, and AWorld. It also adds GPQA comparisons for existing baselines OWL and X-Masters. Figure 3 newly includes MiroThinker in the TRQA comparison, substantially broadening the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New comparisons introduce reported text-only GAIA evaluations for MiroThinker and Tongyi DR, whereas FlowSearch uses the full validation set. FlowSearch's stated benchmark subsets, sample counts, and o4-mini agent roles remain unchanged; no protocol revision explaining its updated scores is documented.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 replaces the generated report for the retained multi-agent AI scientists query, changing the qualitative case-study evidence. The component-ablation design, planner-model study, question-answering trace, and report execution graph remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for FlowSearch's evaluations. Updated point estimates do not establish a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: FlowSearch o4-mini's reported GAIA average changes from 76.96% to 82.42%, including the full-system row in Table 2. HLE text-only/all scores change from 31.60%/30.80% to 36.10%/34.52%. GPQA remains 87.37% and TRQA remains 77.9%. Numerous comparator results are added, including MiroThinker's 64.7% TRQA result; Appendix D.2 also replaces the qualitative report output.

T1.justification: The DAG definition, planning and execution equations, and refinement formulation are retained. Changing the linear-pipeline step symbol from s to a is equivalent notation; no new formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results appear.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the performance claim from state-of-the-art to competitive, and the results discussion narrows HLE leadership to training-free methods. The dynamic knowledge-flow contribution remains intact, while the introduction still claims state-of-the-art results across all four benchmarks.

C2.justification: v2 specifically attributes fragmented reasoning in sequential systems to context truncation and retrieval filtering, expanding v1's context-overflow explanation. It also interprets performance relative to trained agentic models and explicitly qualifies comparisons involving text-only subsets.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly identifies comparator backbones, including Claude-3.7 for MiroFlow and Gemini-2.5-Pro for OWL. The code address changes from Alpha-Innovator/InternAgent to InternScience/InternAgent. Tool descriptions, summarization details, and planner-data construction in Appendices A–C are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix D.2 extensively replaces the generated survey's cited literature with a 65-source bibliography, including MASTER, AOAD-MAT, and Latent-X. This substantial citation change occurs within the example output. The paper's main 44-reference bibliography remains unchanged, while Related Work modestly revises its agent taxonomy.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten, Related Work moves ahead of the method section, and the generated appendix report receives an entirely different narrative and section structure. Author additions, contribution-credit wording, terminology, and several explanatory passages also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves off the title page and changes its displayed comparisons; Figure 3 adds a comparator bar. Table 1 gains a backbone column and additional method groups. Appendix D.2 switches from integrated typesetting to inset report pages with much smaller text and a separate numbered bibliography, removing the former Table 7.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons, disclosed backbones, and explicit subset qualifications make the central benchmark evidence more informative. These benefits support a limited overall improvement. The revised GAIA/HLE scores remain unexplained, broad state-of-the-art claims persist, and the replacement appendix report's much smaller text reduces readability.
